title: Vanishing of even-level Fourier coefficients of odd functions
statement: Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be an odd Boolean function, meaning $f(\lnot x) = -f(x)$ for every $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, where $\lnot x$ denotes the pointwise negation of $x$. Then for every subset $S \subseteq [n]$ of even cardinality, the Fourier--Walsh coefficient of $f$ at $S$ vanishes: $\hat f(S) = 0$.
hypotheses_covered: f is an odd Boolean function (f(¬x) = -f(x) for all x)
replaced: If $f$ is odd and $|S|$ is even, then $\hat f(S) = 0$.
